title: Choir and Wolf
premise: Vesper Amberdale, a mercenary bound by oath to a god who fell silent a century ago, has spent their whole life in the Godless Valley where magic cannot follow — until a date night with the archivist Sable Fenwick turns up their names in a prophecy book written before either was born. Pulled into the prophecy's machinery, they discover the silent god did not die: it was devoured by the thing now wearing King Aldric's crown, and the long winter falling over the realm is its digestion made weather. To break the king's binding, Vesper must choose between the loyalty their oath demands and the truth that their god chose silence to warn them; Sable must choose between preserving history and rewriting it. In the end, Vesper severs the crown's hold at the cost of their own oath-magic, freeing both king and god — but the god, reborn small and mortal, chooses them as its first follower all over again, freely given.
about_author: Dominic Thackeray is a former cathedral chorister turned fantasy novelist who writes about oaths, music, and the people caught between them. He lives in a drafty stone house in the north of England with two indifferent cats and an ever-growing collection of antique hymnals.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Vesper Amberdale, POV. A rare evening off: Vesper takes archivist Sable Fenwick to the valley's autumn fair, awkwardly courting between mercenary drills and honey wine. When Sable shows them a newly catalogued prophecy book for fun, Vesper's own name stares back from a page dated a hundred years past. Emotional beat: warmth curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Ink That Breathes
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The prophecy book pulls them both into its pages mid-sentence. They land a century away in a snowbound capital, wearing clothes that fit too well, recognized by strangers as figures from legend. Emotional beat: disorientation and the first spark of wonder — Sable is thrilled; Vesper is not.

chapters.title: A City Holding Its Breath
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. The capital is under early winter lockdown; the king has not been seen in months, only heard — singing through palace walls at night. Vesper's oath-brand, dormant since the god went silent, begins to ache near the palace. Emotional beat: homesickness sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Heresy
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Sable seeks the restricted royal archive and finds pages razored out of every chronicle covering the year the god fell silent. A librarian warns them that asking about the Silence is treason. Emotional beat: scholarly delight colliding with fear; Sable decides truth is worth the risk.

chapters.title: What the Crown Sings
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Drawn by the ache of their brand, Vesper hears the king's nighttime song and recognizes it: a hymn to their own silent god, sung wrong, syllables inverted. Something is wearing Aldric like a glove. Emotional beat: horror and reluctant compassion for the trapped king.

chapters.title: Company of the Sworn
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Vesper tracks down the last cells of their old order, the Sworn of the Quiet Choir, now hunted heretics led by the scarred Mother Cassia. Cassia reveals the prophecy names Vesper as 'the wolf at the choir door' — savior or destroyer, the text won't say. Emotional beat: homecoming shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: Pages We Shouldn't Have Read
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Decoding the mutilated chronicles, Sable learns the god wasn't killed by enemies — it was fed upon by its own high priest, whose soul became the thing in the crown. The final page names a second reader: Sable themselves. Emotional beat: vertigo; the book knew they were coming.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Begins
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The false winter accelerates — rivers freezing mid-current, birds dropping from the sky. Riots ignite as the Church blames the Sworn. Vesper and Sable are separated in the chaos. Emotional beat: the world narrowing, stakes becoming bodily and immediate.

chapters.title: Prisoner of the Pale Guard
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Captured by the crown's pale-armored guard, Vesper is brought before the Regent-Cardinal — the priest's living descendant and willing accomplice. Offered freedom in exchange for renouncing the Silent One, Vesper refuses and is marked for the king's altar. Emotional beat: defiance kindled under pressure.

chapters.title: The Library Burns
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The Regent's men torch the archive to bury the truth forever. Sable saves one armful of books and a wounded junior librarian, learning in the flames that the prophecy's missing pages were hidden inside the king's own tomb. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Wolf at the Choir Door
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Sable breaks into the palace dungeons using archive knowledge of forgotten passages, finding Vesper half-drained by ritual feeding. Their escape is bought by Mother Cassia's diversionary assault — and her death. Emotional beat: love proven in action; guilt over the cost.

chapters.title: Interlude: What the God Remembers
chapters.summary: The god's fragmented voice, POV. Between chapters of silence, the devoured god dreams in the crown's belly, remembering its priest's betrayal and reaching toward the one warm thread left: Vesper's oath. Emotional beat: sorrowful tenderness; the first hint the god can still be saved.

chapters.title: The Tomb Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Both POVs interwoven. Following Cassia's maps, the pair descends into the frozen royal crypts to find the missing prophecy pages sewn into the dead queen's shroud. They learn the unbinding rite requires a willing oath broken aloud at the crown itself. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread yielding to clarity of purpose.

chapters.title: An Oath Is a Kind of Love
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. On the crypt steps, Vesper confesses what breaking the oath will cost: their strength, their healing, perhaps their identity as a Sworn. Sable offers to stand in — the rite accepts any true vow. Vesper refuses to let Sable pay. Emotional beat: love against duty, stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: The Cardinal's Sermon
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The Regent-Cardinal publicly declares the end times, crowning the hollow king before the starving city to legitimize total rule. Sable, disguised in the crowd, realizes the coronation renewal is when the binding is strongest — and weakest, if interrupted. Emotional beat: cold strategic fury.

chapters.title: Choir of the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Infiltrating the palace as conscripted musicians, Vesper joins the choir forced to sing the inverted hymn, hiding the true melody inside the false one — a counter-song their body remembers from childhood. Emotional beat: terror and grace fused; music as resistance.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Vow
chapters.summary: Both POVs. At the climax of the ceremony, Vesper steps from the choir, speaks their oath aloud, and breaks it — the brand tearing free like a pulled tooth. The crown cracks; the king screams in two voices. The Cardinal unleashes the winter itself as a weapon. Emotional beat: sacrifice as liberation.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Face to face with the priest-thing, now stripped of its vessel, Vesper fights it with no magic at all — just training, stubbornness, and Sable reading the counter-hymn from the rescued pages. The thing unravels into a century of stolen voices, finally released. Emotional beat: exhaustion, pity, victory without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Spring in the Throat of Winter
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The freed god, reborn small and wordless as a grey-eyed child of light, thaws the valley of the city; the real king wakes, diminished and weeping with gratitude and shame. The Church fractures; the Sworn are pardoned. Emotional beat: cautious dawn after long dark.

chapters.title: The First Follower
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. The newborn god comes to Vesper not demanding worship but offering friendship, asking to learn the world anew. Vesper, oathless for the first time, chooses devotion freely rather than by brand. Emotional beat: identity remade on one's own terms.

chapters.title: The Book Closes Itself
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Back in their own century, the pair finds the prophecy book blank except for a final line praising 'the wolf and the reader.' Sable donates it to the archive uncatalogued, keeping one copied page as a private keepsake. Emotional beat: bittersweet closure; history held lightly.

chapters.title: Choir and Wolf
chapters.summary: Both POVs, alternating short passages. Spring fair in the valley again, mirroring chapter one: honey wine, awkward dancing, a small god napping in Vesper's pack. Vester proposes properly; Sable says yes before the question finishes. Emotional beat: earned joy — loyalty, truth, and love finally pointing the same direction.
